claims.summary: In Braun's F2 one-level complete accuracy-3l old-affine setting, for subspaces T_1..T_C with 1 not in T_c such that every proper span of rank>3l(k+1) contains one, ordered with parents b(c)<c, d_c=v-dim T_c and e_c=dim(T_c+T_b(c))-dim T_c when 1 is not in the sum: if N=binom(d_1+k,k)+sum_{c>=2} min{binom(d_c+k,k), e_c binom(d_c+k-1,k-1)} < dim L_k, D>=6l+1, 2k(D+1)-1<=n and 4(k-1)<n, there is no ordinary-PC refutation through degree D; with every dim T_c>3l(k+1) and k<=m, m ln(4C_inc)<=k^2 with C_inc=1+sum min{1,e_c k/(v-r_*+k)} suffices. Contains the published and shared-span counts; for any cover and parents it is at least min_c k/(d_c+k) times the rank-aware shared-span sum of some sub-cover.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer with corrections and a follow-up check, including the antichain limit. The 19-window witness meets the hypotheses but is excluded by the published count at k+1.
claims.rationale: Pays Braun's common-kernel count by span distance along a tree of covering subspaces.
claims.next_action: Find a family the increment count excludes and no recorded count does, or show none exists.

claims.summary: In Braun's setting at a fixed degree D>=6l+1, with K_D=floor((n+1)/(2(D+1)))>=1 the largest k allowed by 2k(D+1)-1<=n, r_D=3l(K_D+1)+1<v-K_D, q_D=exp(-r_D K_D/(v-r_D-K_D)) and M_D=floor(K_D ln(v+1)/q_D)+1, some family of at most M_D distinct proper coordinate blocks of rank r_D (high-rank at every k'<=K_D) has flats with no common nonzero kernel in L_k' for every k'<=K_D: joint kernels of coordinate restrictions are spanned by row-linear monomials meeting every pinned set, and a union bound over at most (v+1)^K_D monomials leaves none. So at degree D no certificate of the common-kernel step excludes it; ln M_D<=ln(K_D ln(v+1)+1)+3K_D^2/m(1+O(1/K_D+K_D/m)), against the published ln(4M)<=K_D^2/m. At l=16, D=107: K_D=303, ln M_D<=12.62 against 1.40.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer in its third check, after a first version (rank just above the threshold at one k) was excluded at k+1 and a second (k=n/4) was compared with a k no degree allows; the fixed-degree form is the reviewer's suggestion, verified by the author.
claims.rationale: Bounds what any joint-rank certificate can add to Braun's common-kernel step at a fixed degree on unrestricted families: about a factor three in ln M plus a logarithmic term.
claims.next_action: Use as the adversarial baseline when testing structured joint-error savings.
